description: Real VB.NET sourced from two MIT-licensed projects (see NOTICE.md): staxrip/staxrip (Criteria.vb verbatim, FrameServer.vb head excerpt) and Wagnard/display-drivers-uninstaller (Win32Native.vb excerpt). Gates the shapes S5 of #6327 actually emits: Class/Module/Structure/Interface containment, Inherits -> EXTENDS (in-tree chain AND an interface extending an external one), class-level Implements -> IMPLEMENTS (in-tree AND external), Imports -> IMPORTS (bare-name and folded SCOPE.External package), and CALLS gated on the paren disambiguator. Deliberately NOT asserted, because these three sources contain none of them: partial-class merge (S7a) and Handles/AddressOf -> REFERENCES (S7b) are implemented but unexercised here. Also gates S7c: member-level `Implements IFoo.Bar` -> IMPLEMENTS on the MEMBER, with via=implements-member, coexisting with the class-level edge rather than replacing it -- FrameServer.vb carries four clauses onto in-tree IFrameServer members and FrameServer.vb and Win32Native.vb one external `IDisposable.Dispose` each. Still a genuine gap: With-block receivers (S7d). Since #6440 it also gates OVERLOAD IDENTITY: Win32Native.vb's two StructPtr.Dispose declarations must be two nodes, the first keeping the bare name and the second discriminated by its parameter-type list, with no phantom self-CALLS between them — and StructPtr.ObjSize, which does not collide, must keep the exact entity id it had before, which is what makes the fix collision-only rather than an identity migration.

expected_entities.note: ReadOnly Property — the Get accessor gets no entity of its own. ALSO THE #6440 OPTION-B CONTROL: StructPtr declares no second ObjSize, so the collision-only discriminator must leave this name — and therefore this entity id — BYTE-IDENTICAL. cmd/grafel/quality_vbnet_overload_6440_test.go pins the literal id recorded before the change. A discriminator on EVERY member (option A) would move it, and that is an identity migration needing an fbversion bump and a global cross-language reindex.

expected_entities.name: StructPtr.Dispose
expected_entities.note: #6440. `Protected Overridable Sub Dispose(ByVal disposing As Boolean)` (:58) — the FIRST of two Dispose overloads in StructPtr, and the one that KEEPS THE BARE NAME. That is not arbitrary: internal/resolve/refs.go's byLocation index is keyed (file, name) and retains a bucket only when it is UNIQUE, while callTarget/memberTarget emit call targets as a bare name with no arity, so if EVERY overload were discriminated no entity would carry the name a same-file call site asks for and those refs would dangle — strictly worse than the merge this replaces. First-in-source-order is chosen because the #4406 dedup already kept the first record, so the survivor's id does not move.

expected_entities.name: StructPtr.Dispose()
expected_entities.note: #6440. `Public Sub Dispose() Implements IDisposable.Dispose` (:79). Before the fix this declaration had NO NODE OF ITS OWN: graph.EntityID hashes (repo, kind, name, source_file) and nothing else, so both overloads hashed identically and the #4406 dedup dropped this one, unioning its edges onto the :58 record. THIS IS THE ENTRY THAT FAILS BEFORE THE FIX AND PASSES AFTER. The discriminator is the declared PARAMETER-TYPE list — empty here, hence the bare `()`. Types rather than an ordinal because an ordinal renumbers every later overload when one is inserted; the full type list rather than arity because same-arity overloads are the common case in real VB.

`NativeServer.OpenFile(path)` (:28). #6454: the receiver `NativeServer` is declared `Private NativeServer As INativeFrameServer` (FrameServer.vb:12) and that interface is declared in the SAME file (:83), so the call binds in-tree off the DECLARED TYPE rather than the receiver's spelling. STILL NOT OVERLOAD-PRECISE, AND #6440 DID NOT CHANGE THAT: #6440 discriminates colliding DECLARATIONS, but callTarget/memberTarget still render a call TARGET as a bare name with no arity, and the bare name now belongs to the first-declared overload. So the edge asserts that the site produced an in-tree CALLS to a member of that name on that type, nothing finer — the member it names is simply no longer a merge of several declarations. (These four INativeFrameServer members are not overloaded at all, so nothing here moved.) BEFORE #6454 THIS SITE PRODUCED NO EDGE AT ALL — classify answered ParenUnknown for every non-Me qualifier, and a non-statement-head ParenUnknown is not a call — so this is a clean addition, not an amendment of a previously-wrong target.

`Dispose(False)` inside Finalize. NARROWED BY #6440: StructPtr's two Dispose overloads no longer fold onto one node — `Dispose(disposing As Boolean)` (:58) keeps the bare name `StructPtr.Dispose` and `Dispose()` (:79) is emitted as `StructPtr.Dispose()`. This edge therefore lands on the Boolean overload, which is the one Finalize actually reaches. It is still not overload-PRECISE by construction — the call target is a bare name with no arity, so it binds to whichever overload holds the bare name — but it is no longer ambiguous between two declarations sharing one node.
`Throw New Exception("failed to create criteria")` — constructor call to an external type.

S7c: `Property Info As ServerInfo Implements IFrameServer.Info`. The edge is anchored on the PROPERTY, and its target is the INTERFACE MEMBER — neither endpoint is shared with the DirectFrameServer -> IFrameServer class-level edge above, which is why the two coexist instead of competing.
S7c on a bracket-escaped name: `ReadOnly Property [Error] As String Implements IFrameServer.Error`. Both ends drop the brackets, so the member binds.
S7c on a ReadOnly Property.

S7c on a Function with a parameter list. `INativeFrameServer` declares a GetFrame of its own in the same file; the target must be the IFrameServer one, so this entry also pins that the dotted prefix is kept rather than resolved by leaf name.

S7c with an EXTERNAL target: `Sub Dispose() Implements IDisposable.Dispose`. #6337 splits the type from the member and binds to a per-member placeholder, distinct from the class-level ext:dotnet:IDisposable node.

The same external clause on a Module-nested class, four levels deep. Pins that member-level emission does not depend on the owner being top-level, and that both member clauses share the one placeholder. #6440 MOVED THE FROM-ENDPOINT: the clause is on the no-arg `Sub Dispose()` (:79), which used to be merged into the :58 Boolean overload — so the graph showed a node whose signature said `Dispose(disposing As Boolean)` while wearing an IMPLEMENTS edge that belongs to a parameterless method. The from_name is now the discriminated `StructPtr.Dispose()`, and THAT amendment is itself a before/after assertion.

forbidden_relationships.note: VB's ternary `If(cond, a, b)` is an operator, not an invocation. Emitting it as CALLS is exactly the phantom-CALLS class the paren disambiguator exists to prevent.

THIS ENTRY PINS A TRADEOFF, NOT A TRUTH. `Value.ToString` (IntCriteria.ValueString, Criteria.vb) is a GENUINE invocation — VB lets you call a no-arg method without parens, and the ideal extractor would emit this CALLS edge. It is forbidden here because S5's paren disambiguator deliberately chooses precision over recall: without a member-access resolver, treating every paren-less dotted name as a call manufactures phantom edges at a rate that swamps the real ones (#6327). Contrast the sibling `PropertyValue.ToString()` in IntCriteria.PropertyString, which IS parenthesised and carries no forbidden entry — that contrast is the point, and it is what makes this guard test the disambiguator rather than the file. IF A FUTURE MEMBER-ACCESS RESOLVER CORRECTLY EMITS THIS EDGE, AMEND THIS ENTRY — do not weaken the resolver to keep the fixture green. A graded fixture that punishes a correct improvement is worse than no fixture for this shape.
`Select Case`/`Case` are keywords; no CALLS edge may be minted from control flow.
Inheritance direction guard: Criteria is the ROOT of the chain. An inverted EXTENDS would still score full recall on the forward edges above.

#6440's phantom self-CALLS, and the sharpest single symptom of the merge. `Dispose()` (:79) calls `Dispose(True)` — a call to the OTHER overload. With both overloads folded onto one node the edge became a method calling ITSELF: a relationship with no counterpart in the source, minted purely by identity collision. VERIFIED PRESENT before the fix (the assertion failed) and absent after. Do not relax this by allowing self-CALLS generally: a genuinely recursive VB method would produce one legitimately, which is why this entry names StructPtr.Dispose specifically rather than forbidding the shape.
